chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ayyam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Take the pebbles of the Jamarat, then go to the furthest Jamarah which is at Aqaba, and throw it from its front, and do not throw it from its top, and say while the pebble is in your hand: 'O Allah, these are my pebbles, so count them for me and raise them in my deeds.'

Then you throw and say with each pebble: 'Allah is the Greatest. O Allah, drive away Satan from me. O Allah, [as] confirmation of Your Book and upon the Sunnah of Your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). O Allah, make it an accepted Hajj, an accepted deed, an appreciated effort, and a forgiven sin.'
And let there be between you and the Jamarah a distance of ten cubits or fifteen cubits.
So when you go to your mount and return from the throwing, say: 'O Allah, in You I have trusted and upon You I have relied, so good is the Lord, good is the Guardian, and good is the Helper.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'And it is recommended that the Jamarat be thrown while in a state of ritual purity.'

key_terms.الْعَقَبَةِ: Aqaba, a specific location in Mina

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications and rituals for throwing pebbles at the Jamarat during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi provides a detailed ritual guide for the Rami al-Jamarat, emphasizing the spiritual significance of casting pebbles as an act of defeating Satan and affirming the Sunnah. It highlights the recommended practice of performing the ritual in a state of purity (Taharah) and specifies the physical distance of ten to fifteen cubits from the Jamarah, reflecting the scholarly tradition of integrating physical action with specific supplications for acceptance and forgiveness.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Take the pebbles (for pelting the) Jamarah, then go to Al-Qaswa Jamarah which is at Aqaba, so pelt it from its front, and do not pelt it from its above, and you should be saying while the pebble is in your hand, ‘O Allahazwj! These are my pebbles, so Count these for me and Raise these in my deeds’.

And you should be saying with each pebble, ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is the Greatest! O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Drive away the Satan<sup>la</sup> from me! O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! In ratification of Your<sup>azwj</sup> Book and upon the Sunnah of Your<sup>azwj</sup> Prophet<sup>saww</sup>. O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Make it to be an Authorised Hajj, and an Acceptable deed, and an Appreciated effort, and a Forgiven sin’.
And let there happen to be in what is between you and the Jamarah, a measurement of ten cubits, or fifteen cubits.

So when you go to your ride and return from the pelting, so say, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! In You<sup>azwj</sup> I trust, and upon You<sup>azwj</sup> do I rely, for You<sup>azwj</sup> are the best Lord<sup>azwj</sup>, and the best Guardian, and the best Helper’.
Heasws said: ‘And it is recommended that you pelt the Jamarah upon cleanliness’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

you can take the pebbles for al-Jamar and go to al- Jamarah al-Quswa’ which is near al-‘ Aqabah. Throw the pebbles on it from its front side and not from above, and when throwing pebbles say, ‘O Allah, these are my pebbles, count them for me and raise them in my deeds.’

Then commence throwing and with each pebble say, ‘Takbir (Allah is great beyond description). O Allah, keep away Satan from me. O Allah, it is to verify Your book and the Sunnah (tradition) of Your Holy Prophet. O Allah, make it a virtuous al-Hajj, an acceptable deed, an appreciated effort, and forgiven sins.’
Keep a distance of ten yards between yourself and al-Jamarah (the pillar) or fifteen yards.
When you return from al-Jamarah say, ‘O Allah, I depend on You, take You as my attorney; You are the best Lord, the best Guardian and the best helper.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘It is preferable to throw the pebbles with a valid Wudu’.’” NOTE: When throwing pebbles one should say the prayers mentioned above.
